chunks: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to his paternal aunt: 'What prevents you from keeping a blessing in your house?' She said: 'O Messenger of Allah, and what is the blessing?' He said: 'A sheep you can milk. For indeed, whoever has in his house a sheep to milk, or an ewe, or a cow to milk — these are all blessings.'

key_terms.بَرَكَة: baraka (blessing/divine grace) — a concept encompassing material abundance, spiritual benefit, and divine favor that can reside in certain objects, animals, or actions
key_terms.تُحْلَبُ: tuhlabhu (to be milked) — the capacity to yield milk is what confers the blessing; an animal kept for milk is a daily provider of sustenance
key_terms.شَاة: sha'a (sheep) — specifically a milkable female sheep; in classical Arabic fiqh and literature, livestock were prized household assets

ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet Muhammad recommend keeping milkable animals at home according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) advises his aunt to keep milkable livestock — sheep, ewe, or cow — as sources of blessing in the home. This teaching reflects the early Muslim emphasis on self-sufficiency and the spiritual as well as practical value of livestock that provide milk for the household. In the agrarian and pastoral Arabian context, such animals represented both material sustenance and divine favor.
